header.working title: Adapting Schouwen Duiveland Agriculture to Salinisation and Water Scarcity towards 2050: Systemic Barriers and National LVVN Policy Levers

question: How do the actors shape the adaptation of arable farming on Schouwen-Duiveland to salinisation and freshwater scarcity?

actors.label: Arable farmers on Schouwen-Duiveland
actors.interest: Enough fresh water when their crops need it, above all as they germinate, to lower their farms' risk or to raise production. Many want to invest in measures that hold fresh water, once the technique, its costs, its risks and its gain in yield are known for the island's conditions; while supply from outside and measures on the island are both still debated, they hold back.
actors.influence: Decide what the island's farmland grows and how each field is drained, irrigated and supplied with water: in 2025, 200 farms registered on the island grew arable crops on 9,094 ha, of the 13,752 ha of farmland of its 240 farms. A measure in the subsoil can serve several neighbouring farms, which collect and tap its water together; the study of the island's farms explored measures for clusters of one to three. Score 5: they decide the adaptation itself.

actors.label: Waterschap Scheldestromen
actors.interest: Safe dikes and dunes first; then an optimal use of the water system, its ditch levels matched to soil and land use, fresh water kept available where it can and fresh groundwater kept in stock, within costs society accepts. It has no task as a supplier of fresh water: measures beyond its regular water management are for the users of the fresh water to pay.
actors.influence: Sets the island's ditch levels in its water level plans (peilbesluiten: Duiveland 2021, Schouwen 2022), matched as far as it can to soil type and land use such as farming, after a process with the people of the area; sets and enforces the rules for farms' groundwater extraction for irrigation in its waterschapsverordening, a notification within limits per hectare and per well, a permit beyond them. Score 5: it decides binding rules for the island's farms.

relations.description: Sets the ditch levels the island's farms drain to, in its water level plans for Schouwen and Duiveland, and the rules for their groundwater extraction for irrigation.
Takes part with the province in the Zeeuws Deltaplan Zoet Water, and sets up with it a network measuring the boundary between fresh and salt groundwater.

actors.label: Gemeente Schouwen-Duiveland
actors.interest: A vital and liveable countryside, with farming, one of the island's main economic pillars, made climate-proof against salinisation, subsidence and extreme weather, and a reliable water system; water basins on farmland fitted into the landscape.
actors.influence: Its council sets the omgevingsplan, since 1 January 2024 the one plan for the use of all land and buildings on the island, farmland included; its executive decides where a farm may build a water basin outside its building plot; it pays part of farms' advice, research and machines for fresh water and climate-proof farming, and leads the Living Lab Schouwen-Duiveland. Score 5: it decides binding plans for the island's farms.

relations.description: Sets in its omgevingsplan what the island's farmland and farm buildings may be used for, and where a farm may build a water basin outside its building plot.
Pays up to half, at most 25,000 euros, of a farm's costs of advice, research and machines for fresh water and climate-proof farming, from the Living Lab.
Leads the Living Lab Schouwen-Duiveland, in which the water board is a core partner.
Leads the Living Lab Schouwen-Duiveland, in which the province is a core partner.
Leads the Living Lab Schouwen-Duiveland, in which ZLTO and its island branch, Agrarisch Schouwen-Duiveland, are core partners.
Carried out with Deltares the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), on storing fresh water in the subsoil.
Carried out with KWR the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), on storing fresh water in the subsoil.
Carried out with Acacia Water the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), on storing fresh water in the subsoil.
Leads the Living Lab Schouwen-Duiveland, in which Delphy is a practice partner.

actors.label: Provincie Zeeland
actors.interest: Keeping agriculture in the delta, for the fertile deltas' part in world food production, and strengthening nature; enough fresh water and good water quality, worked out with stakeholders in the Zeeuws Deltaplan Zoet Water; groundwater extraction in balance with its recharge.
actors.influence: Sets regional water policy and the omgevingsverordening, whose rules reach the water board, the municipalities, residents and businesses, among them instruction rules the water board's water level plans and the municipality's omgevingsplan follow; sets the water board's tasks and rules of organisation and supervises it; grants the permits for groundwater extraction above 150,000 m³ a year, for drinking water and for open soil energy systems. Score 5: it decides binding rules for the island's farms, mostly through the water board's and the municipality's decisions.

relations.description: Sets the water board's area, tasks and rules of organisation by provincial regulation, sets rules in its omgevingsverordening for the water board's water level plans, and supervises it.
Sets instruction rules in its omgevingsverordening that the municipality's omgevingsplan follows, such as the rule on water basins on farmland.
Co-financed, beside an EU contribution, the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), which the municipality leads.

actors.label: Banks lending to the island's farmers
actors.interest: Loans a farm can repay from its cash flow, with its land and other assets as security; an investment whose returns are not yet proven they often count as a risk. In Rabobank's words, to be a partner of the entrepreneur and help farmers invest in sustainability.
actors.influence: Supply 90% of the borrowed capital of Dutch farms (2018), Rabobank about 85% of the lending to the Dutch food and agri sector (2021); they decide whether a farm gets a loan and at what rate, judging more and more by its cash flow and the entrepreneur, as the Basel capital rules steer them towards profitability and liquidity, with land still an important security, and they count sustainability in classifying a borrower. Measured nationally: no source shows the banks' shares on the island. Score 4: they decide credit many of the island's farms depend on, without binding them.

relations.description: Lend to farms: in the Netherlands, 90% of farms' borrowed capital comes from banks, almost 1 million euro of bank loans per arable farm on average in 2018.

actors.label: Buyers and processors of the island's crops
actors.interest: Raw material of the volume and quality their plants and customers need. Cosun Beet Company, owned by its growers as a cooperative, wants the most value from the beet and good long-term returns for its members, its production in balance with its sales; a potato processor secures its supply through contracts that fix a volume and often its price.
actors.influence: Decide what they take from the island's farms, at what price and to what quality. Cosun Beet Company, part of Royal Cosun, the growers' cooperative that also owns the potato processor Aviko, processes all sugar beet grown in the Netherlands: it sets how much beet each member may deliver (for 2026 cut from 100% to 90% of the allocation, after high yields and with sales limited) and advises its growers field by field. The Dutch potato processing industry turns about 4 million tonnes of potatoes a year into frozen products, an estimated 80% of them exported; of the potatoes for the industry, 5 to 10% are sold free and the rest under contract or in a pool (2020), a contract fixing a volume per hectare and often its price, with bonuses for quality and grading and deductions for tare; Aviko, Farm Frites, Lamb Weston/Meijer and McCain are the processors whose contract prices are reported. Measured nationally: no source read shows which buyers take the island's potatoes, onions and vegetables, or their shares there. Score 4: they decide the sales many of the island's farms depend on, without binding them.

relations.description: Cosun Beet Company buys the island's sugar beet, 1,336 ha on 110 farms in 2025, as it processes all beet grown in the Netherlands, from growers who are its members, each up to its allocation; the potato processors buy most of their potatoes under contract or in a pool, measured nationally.

Cosun Beet Company advises its beet growers field by field through its BAS app, from their crop records in Unitip, soil maps and satellite images, in line with the cultivation guide of the IRS, the Dutch sugar beet research centre it works with.

actors.label: ZLTO
actors.interest: The continuity of farming and horticulture and a future for farmers and growers. On the island, more fresh water: in its island branch's words (2023), catching more rain and a collective system that brings fresh water to the island, a pipeline from the Haringvliet shared among the farmers.
actors.influence: The association of 11,500 farmers and growers in Zeeland, Noord-Brabant and Zuid-Gelderland, in 44 local branches that speak for their members to the municipality and the water board; its board appoints the two members for unbuilt land, farmland included, of the water board's general board of 30; it takes the initiative in the plan that carries out the Deltaplan Agrarisch Waterbeheer in Zeeland, with the water board and the province; on the island its branch looks for more fresh water with the municipality and the province, and a report ZLTO commissioned (2023) finds that farming there becomes impossible without more fresh water. Score 3: it shapes the water board's, the municipality's and the province's decisions directly by representing farmers, binding none.

relations.description: Speaks for its members among the island's farmers, through its branch on the island, to the municipality, the water board and the province; its board appoints the water board's two members for unbuilt land, farmland included.

Takes the initiative in the plan that carries out the Deltaplan Agrarisch Waterbeheer in Zeeland, the measures farmers take of their own accord for the water board's water quality and quantity tasks, working with the water board.
Takes the initiative in the plan that carries out the Deltaplan Agrarisch Waterbeheer in Zeeland, working with the province.

actors.label: LVVN
actors.interest: Sustainable, sufficient and safe food on everyone's plate, valuable nature and a vital countryside, for present and future generations. Agriculture, nature and food quality strengthen each other and sometimes chafe; it makes those dilemmas open to discussion and looks for ways forward together with others in society.
actors.influence: Makes national policy, laws and rules for agriculture, fisheries, food and nature, whose compliance the NVWA supervises. Its minister sets the tariffs of the EU's Common Agricultural Policy support in the Netherlands, paid out by RVO to the farms that apply: for 2025, €174 per hectare of basic income support, €50.35 more on a farm's first 40 hectares, and an eco-scheme premium of €60, €100 or €200 per hectare for activities serving climate, soil and air, water, landscape and biodiversity, for a farm that keeps to the CAP's conditionalities. It publishes the Delta Programme with IenW and VRO, has directors on the Bestuurlijk Platform Zoetwater that advises the minister of IenW on the Delta Programme for Fresh Water, and with IenW, Rijkswaterstaat and STOWA had a knowledge programme on salt in agriculture, nature and water management drawn up (2025, €400,000 that year), on the salt tolerance of crops among its questions, carried out with Deltares and KWR among others. Measured nationally: no source read shows its payments on the island. Score 3: it funds the island's farms directly, through the CAP payments.

relations.description: Pays the farms that apply the CAP's income support and eco-scheme premium per hectare, at the tariffs its minister sets (for 2025: €174 basic income support, €50.35 more on the first 40 hectares, €60 to €200 for the eco-scheme), paid out by RVO; measured nationally.

actors.label: IenW
actors.interest: A reachable country with strong dikes, where people stay safe and get from A to B, with clean air, soil and water, its living environment cared for and raw materials used sparingly. For fresh water, the goal it set with the regional governments in 2019: in 2050 the Netherlands is resilient against freshwater shortage.
actors.influence: Responsible for national water policy, the safety, quality and availability of water among it, and for the working of Dutch water management as a whole; manages the main water system, the large rivers, lakes and seas, with Rijkswaterstaat carrying it out; may instruct provinces and water boards on regional water management where international obligations or interests beyond a region require it. Its freshwater policy ranks the uses of water in a shortage by the verdringingsreeks, which every water manager follows: agriculture in the last of its four categories, temporary irrigation of capital-intensive crops one higher. Its minister coordinates the Delta Programme for Fresh Water, which the six freshwater regions carry out, and manages the Delta Fund, which pays all of Rijkswaterstaat's freshwater measures in the main water system and 25% of a region's (up to 50% for innovative ones or those of several regions): just over €58 million for fresh water in 2026; early in 2027 the Rijk and the regions set the measures for 2028–2033. The Delta Programme 2027, which its minister presents to parliament with the Delta Fund's budget, proposes for the south-west delta that the areas with no supply from outside speed up their way to self-sufficiency, with no extra demand on the Hollandsch Diep and Haringvliet. Score 2: it shapes the island's adaptation through the province, the water board and Rijkswaterstaat; no source read shows the Delta Fund paying for a measure on the island.

relations.description: Is responsible for managing the main water system, which Rijkswaterstaat carries out for it.

Ranks the uses of water in a shortage by the verdringingsreeks of its freshwater policy, which every water manager, the water board among them, follows; may instruct water boards on regional water management where international obligations or interests beyond a region require it.

May instruct provinces on regional water management where international obligations or interests beyond a region require it; under the verdringingsreeks a province may rank the uses within its last two categories in its omgevingsverordening, never between them.

Its minister coordinates the Delta Programme for Fresh Water, whose Bestuurlijk Platform Zoetwater seats LVVN's directors beside IenW's, Rijkswaterstaat's and the freshwater regions'; the two ministries publish the Delta Programme with VRO.

actors.label: Rijkswaterstaat
actors.interest: A safe, liveable and reachable Netherlands, worked on together with others; in drought, the little fresh water of the large rivers and lakes divided as well as it can among all who use it.
actors.influence: Manages the main water system for IenW, the large rivers, lakes and seas, the Delta waters outside the island's dikes among them, for national safety and fresh water supply. In drought it judges, as the water board does for its waters, whether water runs short, and divides the fresh water of the Rhine and Meuse through weirs, pumping stations and sluices by the verdringingsreeks. Most of Zeeland lies outside the area it can supply, where users depend on rain and groundwater; the island has no fresh water supplied from outside (the municipality, 2023). A pipeline to the island, which the province had explored (2021), would draw on waters it manages: the Volkerak-Zoommeer, at the Noorder Krammer or the Schelde-Rijnkanaal, or the Haringvliet, the study's most future-proof source. With LVVN, IenW and STOWA it had a knowledge programme on salt in agriculture, nature and water management drawn up (2025). Score 2: it shapes the island's adaptation indirectly, through what a supply route could draw on; none exists.

relations.description: Agreed with Waterschap Scheldestromen, Brabantse Delta and Hollandse Delta a renewed Waterakkoord Volkerak-Zoommeer (2026, for 15 years) on the lake's water management in normal, wet and dry conditions, so that enough fresh water stays available for nature and agriculture.

actors.label: Deltares
actors.interest: Applied research on water and the subsurface, for future, sustainable and safe deltas and a resilient infrastructure.
actors.influence: An independent knowledge institute for applied research on water and the subsurface, working with governments, companies, knowledge institutions, universities and NGOs in the Netherlands and abroad. On the island it carried out, with KWR, Acacia Water, Agrarisch Schouwen-Duiveland and the municipality, the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), paid by the EU's rural development fund, the province and the municipality, whose quickscans gave 13 farmers advice on storing fresh water in the subsoil that fits the farm's soil, groundwater and economics, followed by five feasibility studies for groups of farms; drainage and infiltration, it concludes, can store far more fresh water underground than was thought; it wrote the project's final report for the municipality with KWR, Acacia Water and Buro Waterfront. With Acacia Water, Delphy, the trial farm Rusthoeve and the municipality it had anti-salinisation and double drainage on the low-lying poelgronden of three farms, at Kerkwerve and Dreischor, demonstrated and monitored (drains laid in 2022, closing meeting in 2024), half paid by the EU; with KWR and WUR it carried out LN2050, research on a climate- and water-robust layout of the countryside towards 2050, the island one of its three example areas, for its farmers, ZLTO's island branch and the Zeeland governments, part of the Ministry of Economic Affairs' Knowledge and Innovation Agenda; in 2025 it was among the knowledge institutes carrying out the national knowledge programme on salt. Score 3: the project's advice reached the participating farms directly; no source read says which partner wrote which advice.

actors.label: KWR
actors.interest: Knowledge that lets the water sector operate water-wise in an urbanised society, bridging science and practice.
actors.influence: A knowledge institute of about 210 people, owned through KWH Water B.V. by the Dutch water companies, its shareholders since 2006, and Belgium's De Watergroep since 2016; its customers are water companies, water boards, governments, industry and small businesses. On the island it carried out, with Deltares, Acacia Water, Agrarisch Schouwen-Duiveland and the municipality, the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), paid by the EU's rural development fund, the province and the municipality, whose quickscans gave 13 farmers advice on storing fresh water in the subsoil that fits the farm's soil, groundwater and economics, followed by five feasibility studies for groups of farms; drainage and infiltration, it concludes, can store far more fresh water underground than was thought, and co-wrote its final report for the municipality; with Deltares and WUR it carried out LN2050, research on a climate- and water-robust layout of the countryside towards 2050, the island one of its three example areas, for its farmers, ZLTO's island branch and the Zeeland governments, part of the Ministry of Economic Affairs' Knowledge and Innovation Agenda; in 2025 it was among the knowledge institutes carrying out the national knowledge programme on salt. Score 3: the project's advice reached the participating farms directly; no source read says which partner wrote which advice.

actors.label: Acacia Water
actors.interest: Access to clean and safe fresh water for everyone.
actors.influence: An independent water consultancy, based in Gouda, with 41 employees and work in 19 countries, water for agriculture and groundwater development among its expertise. On the island its hydrologists led farmers in measuring the salinity of the ditches round their fields (Natuurlijk Zoet, 2019–2021, set up with Agrarisch Schouwen-Duiveland and the water board, the results in the water board's database); it carried out, with Deltares, KWR, Agrarisch Schouwen-Duiveland and the municipality, the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), paid by the EU's rural development fund, the province and the municipality, whose quickscans gave 13 farmers advice on storing fresh water in the subsoil that fits the farm's soil, groundwater and economics, followed by five feasibility studies for groups of farms; drainage and infiltration, it concludes, can store far more fresh water underground than was thought, and co-wrote its final report for the municipality; with Deltares, Delphy, the trial farm Rusthoeve and the municipality it had anti-salinisation and double drainage on the low-lying poelgronden of three farms, at Kerkwerve and Dreischor, demonstrated and monitored (drains laid in 2022, closing meeting in 2024), half paid by the EU. Score 3: the project's advice reached the participating farms directly; no source read says which partner wrote which advice.

relations.description: Its hydrologists led the farmers taking part in Natuurlijk Zoet (2019–2021) in measuring the salinity of the ditches round their fields, the results in the water board's database.

actors.label: Delphy
actors.interest: Healthy, successful and sustainable cultivation: better performance for growers, through research, data-driven crop management, advice and training.
actors.influence: A knowledge company, part of Peterson Solutions, with more than 250 professionals active in over 60 countries and its address in Wageningen; its crop experts advise growers in every plant sector, arable farming among them. It is a practice partner of the Living Lab, its manager for arable farming and field vegetables in the south-west and two soil and water experts among the partners, and with Acacia Water, Deltares, the trial farm Rusthoeve and the municipality it had anti-salinisation and double drainage on the low-lying poelgronden of three farms, at Kerkwerve and Dreischor, demonstrated and monitored (drains laid in 2022, closing meeting in 2024), half paid by the EU. Score 2: the demonstrations give data on the techniques' effects; no source read shows it advising the island's farms.
